## Bio

> **Dr. Prashant Kumar Nag** is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Applications at [Galgotias College of Engineering and Technology (GCET)](https://www.galgotiacollege.edu/), Greater Noida, India. He received his Ph.D. in Computer Applications from [Maulana Azad National Institute of Technology (MANIT)](https://www.manit.ac.in/), Bhopal, where his doctoral research focused on designing efficient artificial intelligence and deep learning models for human emotion detection. His research interests include Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing, Affective Computing, Emotion Recognition, Machine Learning, and Healthcare Informatics, with a focus on building intelligent models for understanding human emotions from textual data and applying AI-driven methods to real-world problems. Dr. Nag has qualified the UGC-NET examination four times and received a national research fellowship for his doctoral research. Alongside teaching postgraduate courses in the MCA program, he is actively involved in student mentoring, curriculum development, training and placement activities, career planning initiatives, and outcome-based education practices. He is committed to research-driven teaching, interdisciplinary collaboration, and the development of practical AI solutions for education, healthcare, and society.

## Beyond the Biography

My academic and professional interests extend beyond research publications and classroom teaching. I enjoy exploring how technology can simplify research workflows, improve reproducibility, and create more effective learning experiences.

Much of my work involves integrating different tools and technologies into practical systems for research computing, scholarly writing, teaching, and academic administration.

I am particularly interested in developing reusable solutions, automating repetitive activities, documenting implementation experiences, and sharing practical knowledge with the wider academic community.

## Research & Teaching

My research focuses on developing intelligent computational models for understanding human emotions, particularly through textual data.

I work at the intersection of **Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, Deep Learning, and Affective Computing**, with interests in contextual representation learning, emotion analysis, explainable machine learning, and healthcare applications.

As an educator, I aim to connect theoretical foundations with practical implementation. My teaching approach emphasizes computational thinking, hands-on programming, problem-solving, and the application of emerging technologies to real-world challenges.

I am also interested in developing interactive teaching demonstrations, reproducible course materials, and digital learning environments that make complex concepts more accessible to students.

## Open-Source Development

I believe that academic tools and computational workflows should be **transparent, reusable, reproducible, and accessible**.

This philosophy motivates my interest in developing open-source software, Quarto extensions, academic document templates, and automation utilities.

My development work includes Quarto-based thesis and pre-thesis templates, reproducible documentation systems, and practical tools intended to simplify academic writing, research publishing, teaching, and administration.

I am particularly interested in combining programming, document automation, and reproducible publishing to reduce repetitive academic work and improve consistency.

Developing these tools also provides opportunities to explore new technologies, evaluate alternative approaches, and contribute practical solutions to the academic community.

## My Digital Ecosystem

My academic workflow combines research computing, scholarly writing, software development, automation, and digital content creation.

Rather than relying on a single application, I prefer integrating complementary tools into efficient and reproducible workflows.

The following technologies represent some of the tools and platforms I use across different aspects of my academic and development activities.

| Area | Selected Tools & Technologies |
|---|---|
| **AI & Research Computing** | Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, R |
| **Academic Writing & Literature Management** | Quarto, LaTeX, Zotero, Better BibTeX, Obsidian |
| **Development Environment** | VS Code, Git, GitHub, WSL2, Linux, uv |
| **Research Reproducibility** | Hydra, DVC, GitHub Actions |
| **Academic Automation** | Python, R, Quarto, Google Apps Script |
| **Data Analysis & Visualization** | Pandas, Matplotlib, ggplot2, Plotly |
| **Content Creation & Publishing** | Quarto Websites, Markdown, OBS Studio, GitHub Pages |

The real value of these tools lies not merely in their individual capabilities, but in how they can work together.

For example, a research workflow may begin with literature discovery and reference management in Zotero, continue with analysis and experimentation in Python or R, and conclude with reproducible reports or manuscripts prepared using Quarto.

Similarly, academic automation may involve integrating spreadsheets, scripts, templates, and publishing systems to streamline recurring administrative and teaching tasks.

I document these workflows, including tool selection, configuration, integration, and practical implementation, through ResearchInfuser.

## ResearchInfuser — Learning Through Practice

**[ResearchInfuser](../ResearchInfuser/index.qmd)** is my initiative for documenting and sharing practical knowledge related to academic research, programming, scientific computing, educational technology, and digital productivity.

It grew from my interest in understanding not only how individual tools work, but also how they can be combined to solve real problems encountered by researchers, educators, and students.

Through ResearchInfuser, I aim to share step-by-step tutorials, structured learning paths, video demonstrations, productivity tips, and practical workflow examples.

The content focuses on five interconnected areas:

- **Research & Academic Writing:** Literature management, systematic reviews, scholarly writing, reference management, and reproducible publishing.
- **Programming & Research Computing:** Python, R, development environments, machine learning, data analysis, and reproducible computational workflows.
- **Digital Productivity:** Keyboard shortcuts, automation, software configuration, and techniques for improving everyday digital work.
- **Teaching & Academic Automation:** Interactive educational demonstrations, digital course materials, academic documentation, and administrative automation.
- **Open-Source Development:** Quarto extensions, reusable templates, software development practices, and practical academic tools.

Rather than simply listing software or recommending applications, I aim to explain **why a particular tool is useful, when to use it, how to configure it, and how it integrates into a complete workflow**.

My goal is to make technical knowledge more accessible while encouraging experimentation, reproducibility, and continuous learning.
